selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main qualities did he show while delivering the message and calling people to the truth?
questions.answer: He showed strong determination, firmness, and courage.

questions.question: What kinds of opposition did he face according to the passage?
questions.answer: He faced resistance from powerful governments, other religions, and even from his own people, tribe, and uncle.

questions.question: How did he respond to that opposition?
questions.answer: He did not show fear, panic, or hesitation.

questions.question: What result of his mission is given as evidence of his unique strength in preaching?
questions.answer: He confronted the world successfully and Islam became dominant on a wide scale.

questions.question: How is his faith described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as exceptionally strong, deeply certain, wide in scope, and very elevated.

questions.question: What failed to weaken his faith?
questions.answer: The beliefs, ideas, philosophies, and teachings that were common in the world at that time could not shake it, even with strong hostility.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Companions and other righteous believers of later generations?
questions.answer: It says they drew from his faith and saw him as the highest example of belief.

questions.question: What conclusion did the traveler reach about truthfulness and dishonesty?
questions.answer: He concluded that someone with such unmatched law, religion, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith could not be a liar or deceitful person.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect idea is presented between his qualities and the traveler’s conclusion?
questions.answer: Because his mission produced unmatched results and his faith remained unshaken, the traveler saw this as proof of his honesty.

questions.question: What overall claim does this passage make about him in comparison with others?
questions.answer: It presents him as unequaled in delivering the message and in the strength of his faith.

questions.question: Which close relationships made the opposition especially difficult for him?
questions.answer: His own tribe and his uncle were among those who opposed him.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying he challenged the whole world?
questions.answer: It suggests that his mission was global in impact and that he stood firmly against very great opposition.

questions.question: According to the passage, what made his belief extraordinary besides strength?
questions.answer: It also had deep certainty, broad reach, and lofty conviction.

questions.question: How did the intellectual and religious climate of the time affect him?
questions.answer: It did not create any real doubt or weakness in him.

questions.question: What role do the Companions play in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: They serve as leading examples of believers who recognized the greatness of his faith.

questions.question: How do believers from later ages support the claim being made?
questions.answer: They are said to have taken from his source of faith and accepted him as the highest model of belief.

questions.question: What final judgment does the traveler make about lying and hypocrisy?
questions.answer: He decides that such faults cannot belong to a person with these unmatched spiritual and moral qualities.

questions.question: Which areas of excellence are listed together near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Sacred law, Islam, worship, supplication, calling to truth, and faith.

questions.question: What is the central message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: His unmatched courage and faith prove his truthfulness and sincerity.

questions.question: What two major themes organize this passage?
questions.answer: His firmness in preaching and his unmatched strength of faith.

questions.question: In the passage, what personal traits appear when he invites people to the truth?
questions.answer: He appears brave, steady, and unwavering.

questions.question: What is significant about the fact that even his own people opposed him?
questions.answer: It shows that the pressure against him was not only from outsiders but also from those closest to him.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying he showed no sign of inner disturbance?
questions.answer: It implies that his confidence in his mission was complete.

questions.question: How does the spread and success of Islam function in the argument?
questions.answer: It is presented as evidence that no one else matches him in conveying the message.
